claims.text: AI-credited flaws reach CISA's exploited list no more often than other flaws.

restates.quote: the data does not suggest that AI discovered vulnerabilities are inherently more likely to be exploited than those found through traditional methods.

claims.data_source: CISA KEV and CVE List: AI-credited base rate, records listed within 90 days

claims.text: By the end of 2028, AI-powered malware is used in a ransomware attack on UK critical national infrastructure, as the UK government or the NCSC publicly confirms.

restates.quote: It is highly likely that between now and 2028, AI-powered malware will have been used in a ransomware attack on UK CNI.

claims.data_source: Statements by the UK government and the NCSC

support.text: The UK government or the NCSC states that a ransomware attack on UK critical infrastructure used AI-powered malware

challenge.text: The UK government or the NCSC states that a claimed AI-powered ransomware attack on UK critical infrastructure did not use AI-powered malware

claims.text: The flood of new flaws is lasting, not a passing wave: at the end of 2028 the 13-week count of new CVE records is still at least 300% above (4 times) its 2023 to 2024 average (+432.6% on 8 Nov 2026).
claims.data_source: CVE List: Gap Flood, 13-week count of new CVE records against the 2023 to 2024 mean

claims.text: AI flaw-finding keeps scaling beyond Anthropic: at the end of 2027 the 13-week count of AI-credited flaws excluding Anthropic is at least 450 (224 in the 13 weeks to 8 Nov 2026).
claims.data_source: CVE List: AI-credited CVE records published in 13 weeks, excluding Anthropic (a lower bound)

claims.text: Exploitation speeds up: at the end of 2027 the whole 80% range of the 26-week median days from disclosure to CISA's exploited list is under 15 days (13 to 22 on 8 Nov 2026; 2023 to 2024: 15 to 36).
claims.data_source: CISA KEV and CVE List: Gap Window, 26 weeks, median days after disclosure and its 80% range

claims.text: AI agents prove hard to control: by the end of 2028 an authority in the US, UK, EU, Japan or Taiwan reports a new case of an AI agent causing a breach without its owner's consent.
claims.data_source: Statements by cyber agencies, data protection authorities and other regulators in the US, UK, EU, Japan and Taiwan

support.text: An authority in the US, UK, EU, Japan or Taiwan reports a case, first public after 12 Nov 2026, of an AI agent causing a breach without its owner's consent

challenge.text: An authority in the US, UK, EU, Japan or Taiwan finds that a breach blamed on an AI agent acting without its owner's consent in fact involved no AI agent

claims.text: Unpatched holes get exploited more: Verizon's 2028 Data Breach Investigations Report puts exploited vulnerabilities above 31% of breaches with a known way in (2026 report: 31%).
claims.data_source: Verizon's 2028 Data Breach Investigations Report: exploitation of vulnerabilities among known initial access vectors

support.text: Verizon's 2028 Data Breach Investigations Report puts exploitation of vulnerabilities at more than 31% of known initial access vectors in breaches

challenge.text: Verizon's 2028 Data Breach Investigations Report puts exploitation of vulnerabilities at 31% or less of known initial access vectors in breaches

claims.text: Geopolitics turns AI flaw-finding into a state weapon: by the end of 2028 the US, UK, Japan, Taiwan, the EU or an EU state blames a foreign state for a new intrusion using AI to find or exploit flaws.
claims.data_source: Government attributions, joint advisories, indictments and sanctions notices in the US, UK, EU, Japan and Taiwan

support.text: The US, UK, Japan, Taiwan, the EU or an EU state blames a foreign state for an intrusion made public after 12 Nov 2026 and says AI found or exploited the flaws

challenge.text: After 12 Nov 2026 the US and Chinese governments both commit, jointly or in a shared UN text, to limits on the use of AI in cyberattacks
